memory_update.method_note: Serenity Layer 3 ranking emphasized bottleneck control, AI-capex conversion dependency, supplier/labor scarcity, evidence quality, falsifiability, and risk clarity. Physical infrastructure chokepoints outranked broad enterprise AI software monetization.

items: For EME, verify data-center backlog, mission-critical revenue mix, customer concentration, margin trend, labor constraints, and project-cycle exposure.
For TT, verify AI/data-center cooling revenue, LiquidStack contribution, liquid-cooling attach rates, margin impact, and competitive positioning.
For EQIX, verify AI-related leasing, power availability, utilization, pricing, interconnection growth, and returns on AI-ready capacity.
For CRM, verify AI ARR quality, Agentforce paid adoption, Data 360 expansion, inference-cost impact, and customer ROI.
For NOW, verify paid agentic AI workflow adoption, renewal/expansion impact, AI specialist contribution, and competitive displacement risk.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source validation of AI/data-center share of backlog, incremental order growth from hyperscale or colocation customers, margin contribution from mission-critical work, and whether growth is broad construction inflation or AI-specific bottleneck demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: EMCOR is closest to the AI buildout execution chokepoint in this chunk. If AI data-center capex is constrained by electrical work, mechanical systems, commissioning, substations, labor availability, and project execution rather than only chips, EME is a high-priority candidate. The setup is falsifiable through backlog mix, data-center exposure, margin behavior, labor constraints, project timing, and customer concentration.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need data-center and AI-specific revenue/backlog disclosure, LiquidStack contribution, evidence of attach rates to high-density AI deployments, pricing power, and whether cooling demand is incremental versus general commercial HVAC strength.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Trane maps to the thermal-management layer, where higher AI rack density increases demand for liquid cooling, heat rejection, controls, chillers, and central-plant optimization. The chokepoint is credible because power density and cooling infrastructure can gate deployment of next-generation AI racks. It is less pure than a dedicated liquid-cooling supplier but has stronger scale, customer access, and public-market investability.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer quantification of AI workload contribution, pricing and utilization in AI-ready capacity, power availability by market, interconnection uplift from AI customers, and whether returns on new AI-oriented capacity exceed broader colocation returns.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Equinix has durable exposure to AI-related colocation, interconnection, cloud adjacency, and distributed enterprise infrastructure. It scores high on demand durability and public-market quality, but lower on Serenity bottleneck purity because it is a broad digital-infrastructure platform rather than a narrow supplier of the most constrained AI capacity layer. It remains a strong tracking candidate for whether AI demand spreads from hyperscale campuses into interconnection-rich enterprise and cloud-adjacent facilities.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that AI ARR is incremental rather than repackaged software spend, sustained paid adoption beyond pilots, renewal and expansion impact, gross margin effects from inference costs, and customer ROI evidence.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Salesforce has the strongest stated enterprise AI monetization evidence in the chunk because Agentforce and Data 360 ARR provide measurable adoption signals. However, under the Serenity framework it ranks below infrastructure chokepoints because enterprise AI software is more competitive, less physically constrained, and easier for customers to delay, bundle, or replace. Its value is as a demand-validation signal for enterprise AI rather than a hard supply-chain bottleneck.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source evidence of AI-specific paid adoption, contribution to net expansion, measurable customer workflow automation ROI, AI specialist productivity impact, and whether agentic AI features create pricing power or mainly defend the existing platform.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: ServiceNow is a relevant enterprise workflow and agentic AI candidate, especially if AI adoption monetizes through paid automation, IT operations, service management, and workflow expansion. It ranks fifth because its chokepoint characteristics are weaker than physical infrastructure and cooling, and the candidate chunk flags that more evidence is needed. The thesis is still trackable through AI product attach, paid workflow expansion, renewal behavior, and customer productivity claims.

summary: Within this candidate chunk, Serenity priority favors physical AI-infrastructure chokepoints over broad software monetization. EMCOR ranks first because construction execution, skilled electrical/mechanical labor, commissioning, and mission-critical infrastructure can directly gate AI data-center capacity conversion. Trane ranks second as a cooling and heat-rejection bottleneck tied to rising AI rack density. Equinix ranks third as a durable AI-adjacent digital-infrastructure platform, but its exposure is broader and less bottleneck-pure. Salesforce and ServiceNow have stronger enterprise AI monetization narratives, but lower Serenity chokepoint scores because software-agent adoption is less supply-constrained and easier to contest.
